newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Moscow's MGTS drops France Telecom for payphones.
newsitem.headline: Moscow's MGTS drops France Telecom for payphones.

text.p: Moscow regional telephone company MGTS said on Thursday it no longer wished to cooperate with France Telecom on equipping the Russian capital with public payphones.
"The contract will not be broken. Simply, it will not be prolonged", MGTS spokeswoman Anna Boyko told Reuters.
She said the company had taken such a decision because French payphones were not well enough protected against fraud.
Many Russians use fake telephone cards, causing MGTS big financial losses, she added.
One official at France Telecom, speaking under condition of anonymity, confirmed the Russian move.
"Unfortunately, this is true. But MGTS was not supposed to make it public," he said declining further comment.

"We've asked the French to modify their equipment in order to make it impossible for them to work with fraudulent cards. After several rounds of talks, we eventually decided to have them removed and replaced with Spanish phones which are more efficient against fraud," Boyko said.

OAO Moskovskaya Gorodskaya Telefonnaya Set (MGTS) signed a deal late last year with Spanish telephone group Amper to equip Moscow with 2,000 public telephones by September 1997. About 500 are already in service with the rest due by autumn this year, Boyko said.
Under a contract signed in September 1995, about 300 French public phones were installed in the city's metro and streets.
